ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (No. 35) as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Amendment Act 2022 together with the Companies Act 1993, Income Tax Act 2007, Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, Terrorism Suppression Act 2002, and the associated AML/CFT (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2023 (LI 2023/159).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner / Subscriber Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies in the UBO's home jurisdiction (or New Zealand Companies Office for an existing NZ entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the document originates from a Hague Apostille Convention state: (1) Notarization by a local notary; (2) Apostille issued by the competent authority of that state; no further consular legalization. If from a non-member state: (1) Notarization; (2) Consular Legalization through the nearest New Zealand embassy or consulate. Never chain both paths sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Non-Compliance / Extract from Home Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction corporate registry, for foreign UBO entities; or New Zealand Companies Office if the shareholder is a domestic company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing registry sits in an Apostille Convention country: notarize, then apostille via the designated local competent authority; otherwise, notarize and perform consular legalization at the New Zealand diplomatic post responsible for the country of issuance. The two authentication procedures are parallel, mutually exclusive, and never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the New Zealand incorporation agent and approving the formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner / Shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille member state: executive certificate of board resolution notarized and apostilled. For a non-member state: notarization followed by consular legalization at the New Zealand embassy or consulate with jurisdiction over the place of execution. Sequential chaining of apostille and consular legalization is expressly prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Constitution) of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner / Subscriber Company or Draft New Zealand Constitution for the subject NZ_LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder assembly or originating corporate registry; for the proposed NZ_LTD, the New Zealand Companies Office / incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If from an Apostille state: certified true copy from the issuing authority or notarized copy plus apostille. If from a non-member state: notarized copy plus consular legalization before the New Zealand consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Bankability and Source of Funds Comfort Letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A regulated commercial bank holding the UBO's / subscribing company's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For the issuing bank in an Apostille Convention signatory: bank manager's notarized signature then apostille by the competent central distributing office. For banks located in non-signatory states: notarized bank signature followed by consular legalization at the New Zealand consulate with existing consular authority. The two routes cannot be mixed or applied in sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, authorised signatories, and commercial counterparties must be screened before incorporation against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the New Zealand autonomous sanctions regulations under the Sanctions Act 2019, and the FCO/Registrar watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any PEP, family member of a PEP, or close associate is identified, requiring documented senior management approval, ongoing transaction monitoring, and re-screening at minimum every six months. The screening outcome must be recorded in an audit-ready file and retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Name Search and Online Company Registration portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be presented in Latin script (A-Z, 0-9) with permitted punctuation only; te reo Maori names are accepted if the meaning is lawful and not misleading. A name in non-Latin script must be transliterated into English phonetic equivalent and, where relevant, the Registrar may request a translation to confirm the absence of a prohibited meaning. The four-tier naming convention applies: (1) exact match – rejected if identical; (2) similarity – rejected if nearly identical or likely to confuse; (3) prohibited token – requires ministerial/regulator consent; and (4) permitted with conditions – name allowed only after specific statutory approval is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant has no automatic right to a formal extension of the name hold under Companies Register practice; instead the applicant may submit a fresh name application immediately after correcting the non-compliant component. An administrative appeal may be lodged within 20 working days of the refusal by emailing the Companies Office at appeals@companiesoffice.govt.nz with a detailed written submission, annexing evidence of legal entitlement to the name, proposed articles, and a legal opinion showing the absence of deception. The Registrar must respond in writing within 15 working days, and further judicial review is available in the High Court only after exhausting this registry-level appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or serviced suite at a physical New Zealand street address is permissible for registered office and service-of-process purpose, provided it is a genuine, staffed location where the company's address-for-service is physically maintained and mail is accepted and forwarded. However, a commercial mailbox, PO Box, or purely digital location is rejected for both Inland Revenue registration and banking KYC. For an ISIC 5820 social casino/publishing business, the local tax authority and customer due diligence expectations of tier-1 banks will require additional commercial substance indicators such as an actual operational office, a local compliance officer, and a physical board meeting space, making the bare virtual office model high-risk for account approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) valid verified address in the Companies Register; (2) physical street signage matching the registered name; (3) on-site availability of corporate records during business hours; (4) no diversion of mail to a private residence; (5) documented rent or service agreement. Quantified risk: Low-to-moderate, estimated 5-10% per year for a simple online software publisher, rising to 20% if the registered office is a shared virtual director mailbox or the sector is classified as ML/TF-sensitive.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), including sections 12-19 (registration of companies), 21-23 (company names), 148-151 (directors), 186-187 (registered office and records), and the Companies (Share Capital and Acquisition by Company of its Own Shares) Regulations 2008
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Government of New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (online incorporation form submitted through the New Zealand Companies Office register)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement is imposed on a New Zealand limited company. The company may be incorporated with a single ordinary share subscribed for NZD 1.00. There is no statutory escrow account or capital deposit requirement. At least one director must ordinarily reside in New Zealand or Australia under the relevant reciprocity provisions, and a registered office must be maintained in New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, effective as of the date of this resolution, that the Company's share capital under the Companies Act 1993 shall be fixed at NZD 1.00, divided into one ordinary share of no par value, and that such share be allotted and issued fully paid to the founding subscriber named in the incorporation application, with the subscription consideration to be recorded in the Company's share register. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company in New Zealand, as specified in the Application for Registration, is hereby adopted, and that the Company's address for service and records location shall conform with sections 186 and 187 of the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED that the persons named below, each having consented in writing and being eligible under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993, are appointed directors of the Company: [Full Legal Names]. Further, [Name] is appointed Managing Director and [Name] is appointed Corporate Compliance Officer, with authority to execute banking mandates, licensing filings, and all incidental corporate instruments. RESOLVED that the board approves the opening of a corporate bank account and that any two directors jointly, or one director and the Compliance Officer, shall be authorised signatories on behalf of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand (online company search and name reservation facility at companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing reserved or registered name and does not contain restricted words, such as 'Bank', 'Trust', or 'Insurance', without the prior consent of the relevant regulator. File an application for name reservation through the Companies Office online portal if a period of marketing or pre-incorporation preparation requires exclusivity. The name reservation is provisional and does not by itself confer incorporation.
required_dossiers: Evidence of authority to use any restricted word or regulated industry term, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is rejected, the applicant shall receive an electronic notice stating the grounds of refusal. The applicant may file a new name application with alternative names or make representations to the Registrar for reconsideration under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. Any third-party objection to a similar name may be resolved by filing a fresh application or by court order in Trade Mark or Fair Trading disputes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution, Shareholder Subscriptions, and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company legal counsel and founding shareholders; notarization not required for domestic incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution or resolve to rely on the default rules in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993. If a constitution is adopted, it must be signed by each shareholder and retained with company records. Obtain written consent from each proposed director under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993, confirming eligibility and acceptance of office. Prepare a shareholders agreement or subscription declaration specifying the allotment of one ordinary share at NZD 1.00. Confirm the New Zealand registered office address and address for service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or company counsel identifies deficiencies in the constitution, consent forms, or registered office address, the documents must be corrected and re-executed. Defective director consents may be cured by obtaining a fresh witnessed signature and lodging it with the company records; any dispute among founding shareholders may be resolved by a revised subscription agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Online Application for Registration of a Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, MBIE (online incorporation portal through the New Zealand Companies Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Application for Registration of a Company via the Companies Office digital channel. Enter the proposed name or select the previously reserved name, state whether a constitution is adopted, provide the particulars of directors and shareholders, specify the share structure and consideration, and register the New Zealand registered office and address for service. Electronically attest the accuracy of the information. No physical notarization is required for online submission, but every director consent and shareholder subscription must be retained and available for inspection.
required_dossiers: Director consents and personal identification data
Registered office address and service address details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a query or issues a notice of defective application, the applicant must respond electronically through the Companies Office portal within the prescribed period, usually 20 working days. Corrections to director, shareholder, or address details may be made by filing a formal rectification request or by resubmitting the application with amended particulars. If the application is refused, the applicant may apply to the High Court for review or file a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Statutory Filing Fee and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, MBIE (online payment gateway and electronic registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the prescribed registration fee electronically by corporate credit card, debit card, or approved online banking facility. Upon successful payment and validation of the application, the Companies Office will issue the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and allocate a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Verify that the certificate states the company number, incorporation date, legal name, and jurisdiction. The certificate serves as conclusive evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: NZBN notification from the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is declined or the certificate is not generated due to a technical failure, the applicant should verify the payment status with the bank and contact the Companies Office contact centre for manual issuance. If the certificate contains a clerical error, request a corrected certificate through the online register amendment service with no additional incorporation filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Corporatization, Officer Appointments, and Tax Registry Preparations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Companies Office; Inland Revenue for initial tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first formal board meeting, adopt the first board resolution, issue share certificates, and open a corporate bank account. Update any director or officer details in the Companies Register and prepare a company seal if required by the constitution. Register for an IRD number with Inland Revenue and determine whether GST registration is mandatory or optional based on expected turnover under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Obtain an address for service for tax notices and prepare the company records for statutory inspection.
required_dossiers: Minutes and resolutions of the first board meeting
Share certificates issued to founding shareholder
IRD number registration form (IRD 484 or equivalent online application)
GST registration assessment and application if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or a regulator queries the board resolution or officer authority, the company may pass a subsequent board resolution confirming the appointment and provide a certified extract. Any late registration of an officer change may be rectified online, and late tax registration penalties may be remitted by Inland Revenue upon a demonstration of reasonable cause or immaterial inadvertence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board mandate applies because the company operates as a digital software publisher with no manufacturing, extraction, or physical processing facilities. For any incidental office-leasing activity, the relevant authorities are the local city or district council under the Building Act 2004 and the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) for life safety compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license or manufacturing permit is required for publishing or distributing simulated social casino and virtual slots games. The absence of real-money wagering, cash prizes, or physical gambling infrastructure places the activity outside the class 4 gaming licensing regime of the Gambling Act 2003; however the Department of Internal Affairs retains oversight if the platform were later expanded to prohibited wagering models.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Registration not required. The digital publishing activity has no physical premises, no resource consent trigger, and no discharge or emission profile; accordingly no assessment of environmental effects or EIA application is required under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated. If the company later leases office space, the workplace must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 ventilation and indoor air quality guidelines, and any electronic waste from office equipment must be disposed of through a certified e-waste recycler under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any occupied office premises, the building owner must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004, including compliance with the approved fire safety design. The company must obtain a fire evacuation scheme approved by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) if workforce numbers exceed the statutory threshold, complete a health and safety workplace induction for all personnel, and certify electrical equipment under the Electricity Act 1992. No additional civil defense clearance is required solely for the digital publishing of social casino content.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (also known as Inland Revenue), Wellington, New Zealand. Primary compliance portal: myIR secure online services available at www.ird.govt.nz. Corporate registration is administered by the New Zealand Companies Office under the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, which issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Physical export declarations are administered by the New Zealand Customs Service. No sub-national tax authorities exist because New Zealand is a unitary national tax jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the NZ_LTD via the New Zealand Companies Office online register to obtain the NZBN. Step 2: Apply for an IRD number as part of the incorporation process; the IRD number is the single statutory tax identification number used for income tax, GST, PAYE, and FBT. Step 3: Register for GST through myIR when taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, or elect voluntary registration; the IRD number itself serves as the GST registration number. The effective date of GST registration may be backdated to the date the threshold was exceeded. Step 4: For an overseas company carrying on business in New Zealand, first register as an overseas company under the Companies Act 1993 via the Companies Office, appoint a New Zealand resident agent for service of process, file certified constitutional documents (certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles), and then obtain an NZBN and IRD number through the Companies Office registration process. Step 5: A non-resident company with no New Zealand physical presence that supplies remote services (including digital gaming platforms, simulated social casino software, and virtual slots content) to New Zealand consumers must separately register under the remote services GST rules through myIR once annual supplies exceed NZD 60,000; no New Zealand incorporation is required for this specific GST registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A New Zealand limited liability company is a separate income tax taxpayer subject to 28% corporate income tax on worldwide income, with foreign tax credits available for foreign-source income. New Zealand operates a full imputation system: corporate tax is a final entity-level charge, and resident shareholders receive imputation credits attached to dividends to relieve double taxation. There is no default pass-through treatment for a limited company, and no US-style check-the-box classification exists in New Zealand law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under sections HB 1 to HB 15 of the Income Tax Act 2007, available only to a close company with five or fewer shareholders (all individuals or eligible trustees), which causes profits, losses, deductions, and tax credits to flow through to shareholders on a look-through basis, thereby converting entity-level taxation into a pass-through model. (b) Imputation credit account election under Part OB of the Income Tax Act 2007 to maintain an imputation credit account and attach imputation credits to dividends. (c) Consolidated group election under Part IG of the Income Tax Act 2007 for a wholly owned group of New Zealand companies to file a single consolidated income tax return. (d) GST elections under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including the payments basis accounting election under section 19, the default invoice basis, the GST grouping election under section 55, and special output tax apportionment methods approved by the Commissioner. (e) Hybrid and branch mismatch rules under sections FH 1 to FH 15 of the Income Tax Act 2007 impose mandatory adjustment regimes rather than elective check-the-box treatment; however, the ordering rules and defensive adjustment provisions contain taxpayer elections that must be documented contemporaneously.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of total taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) in any consecutive 12-month period; registration is mandatory upon exceeding the threshold and voluntary below it. Non-resident suppliers of remote services, including digital software, simulated social casino platforms, and virtual slots content, are subject to the same NZD 60,000 threshold; once registered, 15% GST must be charged on supplies made to New Zealand resident consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or tax authority pre-approval system for invoices. E-invoicing is voluntary and uses the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 specifications through the accredited New Zealand e-Invoicing network; there is no legislation mandating e-invoicing or API-based clearance of individual transactions. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR on a monthly basis for large taxpayers with turnover exceeding NZD 24 million, on a two-monthly basis as the default, or on a six-monthly basis for smaller suppliers. A GST-registered supplier must issue a tax invoice within 28 days of a business-to-business supply; for business-to-consumer remote supplies, no tax invoice is required unless requested by the recipient. Source documents, including electronic invoicing transaction data, must be retained for seven years. For ISIC 5820 simulated social casino and virtual slots publishing, Apple App Store and Google Play Billing settlement statements constitute the primary transactional evidence for GST return preparation, output tax calculation, and audit substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under sections 11 and 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. For goods: supplies of goods exported by the supplier within 28 days of supply, or goods entered for overseas export by the recipient, are zero-rated. For services: supplies made to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed are zero-rated, provided the services are not supplied directly in connection with land in New Zealand, goods in New Zealand, or other excluded circumstances. Remote services, defined to include digital content, software, and electronically supplied gaming services, are zero-rated when the customer is a non-resident and is outside New Zealand at the time of supply. For NZ_LTD social casino and virtual slots publishing, revenue collected through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing is zero-rated when the playing consumer is a non-resident located outside New Zealand; contemporaneous geolocation records must substantiate offshore consumption. Supplies to New Zealand resident consumers are taxable at 15% GST, and the tax is due on the gross retail consideration before deduction of the App Store or Google Play commission.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service export entry; applicable only to physical goods, not to digital software or remote services; required if any physical merchandise such as branded cards or hardware is separately exported)

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (required only for physical exports; for digital simulation software, substitute with content delivery network logs, hosting platform records, and Apple and Google download records)

Inward Remittance Certificate (not a New Zealand statutory customs or tax document; for digital services, substitute with bank statements evidencing foreign currency receipts, Apple IAP and Google Play Billing payout reports, and monthly revenue reconciliation schedules)
Non-resident recipient declaration or GST zero-rating certificate confirming the customer's offshore status and location
IP address logs, geolocation records, and user account data demonstrating end-consumer consumption outside New Zealand
Tax invoices and settlement reports evidencing the supply value and the zero-rating treatment applied in the relevant GST return
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess erroneously zero-rated supplies retrospectively within four years from the filing date, with no time limit where evasion or fraud is established. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply at 20% for an unapproved tax position taken without a reasonable basis or for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or a similar offence. Use-of-money interest accrues on unpaid GST from the statutory due date until full payment. Fraudulently claiming zero-rating on New Zealand resident digital gaming consumers, fabricating export documentation, or misstating end-user locations constitutes an offence under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, carrying imprisonment for up to five years and fines up to NZD 50,000 for individuals, and fines up to NZD 100,000 for a company. The Commissioner has extended audit powers to require App Store and Google Play payout statements, to reconstruct supplies, to disregard sham or artificial arrangements, and to cancel GST registration where export substantiation is defective. New Zealand does not impose a statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is applied as a transfer-pricing and income-recognition standard consistent with OECD guidance and Inland Revenue administrative practice for remote-services revenue attribution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current and capital account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no exchange controls, no central bank approval requirements for ordinary cross-border transfers, and no restrictions on foreign ownership of a New Zealand limited company. Profit repatriation is permitted freely, but cross-border dividends or interest may be subject to New Zealand withholding tax or approved issuer levy; substantive tax planning documentation is required to minimize treaty leakage.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation period for export proceeds. Exporters may freely retain and use foreign currency receipts in any approved bank. The only compliance layer is the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, which obliges reporting entities to maintain transaction records and report suspicious activity; ordinary export receipts are not subject to exchange control or settlement reporting to the central bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low Feasibility for primary treasury operations. Offshore digital EMI providers cannot obtain a New Zealand banking license or direct access to the local clear stream settlement system; they are not substitutes for a registered New Zealand bank. They may be used only as auxiliary payment conduits in narrowly defined corridors, subject to strict AML counterparty diligence and prohibition on becoming the main treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under the AML/CFT Act 2009; there is no statutory requirement for directors to appear physically at a bank branch. In practice, the larger tier-one banks require a remote video interview plus certified passport, proof of address, and beneficial ownership documentation for non-resident directors. Physical presence can be waived where an independent professional legal or accounting firm certifies identity and verifies source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with trust or nominee opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Companies Office extract, registered share register, full trust deed, source of funds and source of wealth declarations, certified passport copies, independent legal opinion verifying ultimate beneficial ownership, and audited group financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Simulated social casino product lacking a statutory gambling license
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal memorandum under the Gambling Act 2003 confirming that virtual slots and social casino play do not constitute real-money gambling, product certification showing no cash redemption of virtual chips, RNG fairness certificate, player terms prohibiting real-money prizes, and jurisdiction geoblocking controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume in-app purchase revenue from Apple and Google stores
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Store payout statements from Apple and Google, app store analytics dashboard, twelve months of bank statements, New Zealand Inland Revenue tax clearance, written AML/CFT policy, and transaction monitoring system documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctioned or high-risk payment jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enterprise-wide sanctions screening policy, IP geolocation and geo-blocking evidence, adverse media check reports, complete counterparty due diligence records, and an independent compliance audit report confirming effective restrictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the overseas parent or shareholder account to a tier-one New Zealand bank account. The remitter must reference the New Zealand company registration number and the underlying share subscription or capital contribution document. If required by the correspondent bank, the purpose code should identify an inward direct investment or intercompany capital contribution. No Reserve Bank of New Zealand approval is required for ordinary injective capital; however, an Overseas Investment Act 2005 assessment is necessary if the transaction involves sensitive land, fishing quota, or significant business assets. The receiving New Zealand bank will verify beneficial ownership and source of funds before crediting the account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should use the New Zealand Exchange Settlement Account System for domestic NZD payments, SWIFT MT202 and MT103 for cross-border vendor settlements, and commercial letters of credit for high-value inventory imports. The payments can be executed in NZD, USD, or other major currencies through global correspondent banks. There is no exchange surrender obligation and no requirement to obtain central bank approval for outward disbursements. For foreign exchange trades, settlement via CLS is available for NZD and reduces counterparty settlement risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the New Zealand Companies Register (online annual confirmation of company details and shareholder information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 working days after the company's annual confirmation date (usually the anniversary of incorporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Strict-liability offence under the Companies Act 1993; maximum fine up to NZD 10,000. Continued non-filing for three consecutive years enables the Registrar to give public notice and strike the company off the register, vesting all assets with the Crown absent court restoration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements and auditor's report for large companies or other entities required to file under the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (delivered concurrently with the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with the Annual Return, generally not later than the Annual Return filing date; for a 31 March balance date this is normally 7 October
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Enforcement by the Registrar, including court orders to compel filing; fines against the company and each director for ongoing non-compliance; continuing default may support strike-off or liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) for the preceding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, due by the 7th day of the 7th month after balance date (7 October); extended tax-agent due dates may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994, escalating penalty assessments, late payment penalties, use-of-money interest, debt recovery action, and prosecution for serious disregard.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST returns and payment for the applicable GST filing cycle (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment and return due by the 28th day of the month following the end of each taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties, late payment penalties, and use-of-money interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994; persistent non-compliance may trigger IRD enforcement, garnishee action, and potential criminal prosecution for evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven corporate updates requiring confirmation during the annual maintenance cycle (e.g., director, shareholder, registered office, and share structure changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office and, where relevant, Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days of each relevant corporate change; any outstanding changes must be reflected in the next Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Falling to update the register may result in compliance notices, penalties under the Companies Act 1993 for director breach, and inaccuracy of the public register; serious failures may support removal of the company from the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory audit applies if the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, meaning at least two of three thresholds are exceeded: total assets over NZD 20 million, total revenue over NZD 10 million, and 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. Audit is also required if the company is part of a reporting group required to file audited consolidated financial statements, or if shareholder direction or other statutory circumstances mandate an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (NZ IFRS) applies for Tier 1 entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime applies for Tier 2 entities; the New Zealand Special Purpose Framework applies for small companies not required to general-purpose financial reporting. For New Zealand companies, the full set of rules is issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB) under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not require a separate annual UBO return. Ultimate ownership and shareholder details are confirmed through the Annual Return filed with the Registrar of Companies. All share transfers, allotments, and transfers of beneficial interest must be entered in the Register of Members promptly, and director and shareholder changes must be notified to the Companies Office within 20 working days. The registered office must ensure that false or incomplete shareholder disclosure is not submitted on the Annual Return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 to USD 1,000 per annum for a New Zealand registered office and company secretarial support provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to USD 35,000 per annum, depending on transaction volume, subsidiary consolidation, and audit complexity
